title: How Web Data Infrastructure Powers the Next Generation of AI — Patricija Žemaitytė, Oxylabs
talk_summary: A product manager at Oxylabs recounts three war stories of building web-scraping infrastructure: adapting a video API to client needs, redesigning a SERP scraper from 4s to sub-second latency, and scaling a proxy scraper from 10k to 60k requests/sec. The recurring lesson is that infrastructure wins come from repeated adaptation and small latency cuts, not breakthroughs.

takeaways.technique: Organic-data load testing over synthetic traffic
takeaways.what_they_do: They found synthetic load tests easy but uninformative; the real bottleneck was generating traffic that behaves like real client usage, and they eventually accepted production traffic as the only true test.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the hardest part, organic data testing. That means processing traffic that behave enough like real client usage
takeaways.numbers: hit a wall around 20,000 requests/sec in load tests

takeaways.technique: Latency budget hunting across every stage
takeaways.what_they_do: When browsers forced 4s latency against a sub-second target, they audited every stage (layouts, parsers, sessions, proxies) and shaved time incrementally rather than seeking one big win.

takeaways.technique: Scope-cutting for the consumer's actual need
takeaways.what_they_do: Their fast search API dropped ads, widgets, rich results and heavy layouts, keeping only organic/news results that AI systems actually use, which enabled the latency target.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it focuses on the things that actually matters only for AI systems. So, it's mostly organic results, top stories, news, and it cuts away all the heavy layout.

takeaways.technique: Iterate product scope from real client feedback
takeaways.what_they_do: Each client request (transcripts, subtitles, search, metadata) was folded into a growing product suite rather than treated as a one-off, turning a single feature into a family in ~3 months.
takeaways.numbers: ~3 months to full video API suite

takeaways.technique: Observability as part of the load
takeaways.what_they_do: At high scale they recognized telemetry itself becomes load and complexity, so they scaled gradually and accepted production as the real test.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the telemetry itself becomes a part of the load and a part of the complexity
